### Overview:

-   The `web_scraper.R` script has been iterated on such that it is able to extract publications. Data was actually already stored under `pages` as an XML after running the `read_html()` function from the `rvest` package.

-   So there was no need to look further into using other packages and functions to interact with the webpages through R.

-   Additionally used the provided `fetch_researchers.qmd` file to assist with iteration of script. Further code simplification has been made.

    -   Initially was using string detection to extract information containing the subheading title of the publication. Encountered issues where it was grabbing everything that containing that word. Now have changed it so it goes through a for loop of section headings from `h1` to `h6`. If one of those headings contains the "Journals", it grabs the text and returns it.

    -   This was initially done as a function for one type of publication. Then reitterated to be more modular and automatic by giving it a list of publications it runs through. Additionally, if else cases for when there is nothing have been added.

    -   As a result of these changes, the code to grab the names of each researcher was slightly modified. Just made into a new function with it's own if else case statements

-   Outputted the cleaned up data as a `.csv` file with the `urls` and `pages` column omitted as saving as another file type manipulates the XML into an unusable state. This file is uploaded to the [github repository](https://github.com/Simon-a1740071/MATHS-3901-Repo) and can be downloaded and used in other languages.

    -   Now under the publication columns, say "Journals". It lists a string of text starting with "Year Citation XXXX". Then after the first journal entry, all other entries are separated by a bracketed year. e.g. "(2015) journal text".
